title: HubSpot Workflows + Properties Spec (PLG-to-Sales Signal Routing) — v1
body:
Doc purpose
This spec defines the HubSpot CRM configuration required to support the PLG-to-sales signal routing pipeline (telemetry → aggregation/scoring → HubSpot). It covers:
- Custom properties (Company + optional Custom Object)
- Lists/views for triage
- Workflows and task templates
- Required HubSpot API scopes + implementation guardrails
- Ops implementation checklist + validation steps

Audience
- HubSpot Admin / Biz Systems (David Kim)
- Sales Ops (Isabelle Laurent)
- Marketing Ops (Tyler Benson)
- Growth/PLG (Ben Carter)
- Stakeholder reviewers: Sales leadership (Stephanie Nguyen), CS (Jasmine Liu), SE (Markus Klein), Security/Privacy (Dr. Aisha Rahman / Marcus Lin)

Status / current decisions
- We will ship MVP using Company properties + timeline notes + tasks.
- We will not rely on HubSpot sequences for the initial pilot (tasks/templates only).
- We will keep customer-level telemetry out of HubSpot. HubSpot will only store aggregated signals, classifications, and minimal metadata needed for follow-up.
- Ownership must preserve existing owners (esp. CSM-owned accounts / active opportunities). If no owner, use region mapping; if no region mapping, round-robin pool per pilot rules.

Definitions
- PLG signal: A qualified (or near-qualified) “sales-worthy” event derived from self-serve usage and/or intent (docs/pricing/security).
- Signal types (non-exhaustive): scale (sustained volume/spend velocity), reliability (repeated 429s, latency errors), compliance (security docs views, VPC/Private docs intent), expansion (multi-workspace/team growth).
- Signal windowing: daily aggregation; qualification uses last-7d / last-30d windows depending on signal type.

HubSpot data model (MVP)
Option A (MVP): Company-only
- Store a compact, human-readable last signal summary + key numeric rollups directly on the Company record.
- Add timeline events (notes) per routed signal (one per deduped signal key per suppression window).
- Create a follow-up task assigned to the owner (AE/SDR) with due date and template based on signal type.

Option B (Post-MVP): Custom Object “PLG Signal”
- Track each signal as a record with properties; associate to Company + primary Contact.
- Use for reporting attribution and suppression logic inside HubSpot.

We will implement Option A for pilot and keep schema compatible with Option B.

1) Company properties (create in HubSpot)
Property group: “PLG Signals (Redwood)”

Core routing + summary properties
1. ri_plg_signal_last_seen_at
- Type: datetime
- Description: Timestamp of the most recent routed signal (as written by router service).
- Example: 2025-05-27T18:42:11Z

2. ri_plg_signal_last_type
- Type: enumeration (single-select)
- Allowed values:
  - scale_usage
  - scale_spend_velocity
  - reliability_429s
  - reliability_latency
  - intent_dedicated_docs
  - intent_private_vpc_docs
  - intent_security_faq
  - intent_pricing
  - expansion_workspaces
  - expansion_org_invites
  - other
- Notes: keep values stable for reporting. Add new types via change request (see “Change control”).

3. ri_plg_signal_last_summary
- Type: multi-line text
- Description: Human-friendly summary for AEs. Keep < 500 chars where possible.
- Example: “Sustained token growth (7d avg +38% WoW), 12× 429s in last 48h. Dedicated docs viewed 3×. Recommend Dedicated eval + batching guidance.”

4. ri_plg_signal_score
- Type: number
- Description: 0–100 score from scoring service. Used for sorting/triage; not a hard gate in HubSpot.

5. ri_plg_signal_confidence
- Type: enumeration (single-select)
- Values: low | medium | high
- Description: Router-provided confidence (ties to suppression rules; low should not auto-create tasks in pilot unless whitelisted).

6. ri_plg_signal_qualified
- Type: boolean
- Description: True when signal met routing threshold and task was created.

7. ri_plg_signal_suppressed_until
- Type: datetime
- Description: If suppression active, do not create tasks; still allow property updates and timeline note if needed (pilot decision: no note for suppressed; only metrics).

8. ri_plg_signal_suppression_reason
- Type: enumeration (single-select)
- Values:
  - recently_contacted
  - active_open_opp
  - existing_csm_owner
  - marketing_nurture_conflict
  - internal_test_org
  - low_confidence
  - customer_opt_out
  - hubspot_rate_limit_backoff
  - other

9. ri_plg_signal_next_step
- Type: enumeration (single-select)
- Values:
  - create_task
  - notify_csm
  - monitor_only
  - no_action
- Description: Router recommendation; actual action still controlled by workflows.

10. ri_plg_signal_owner_rule
- Type: multi-line text
- Description: Debug string written by router (“preserve_owner: true”, “region: NA”, “rr_pool: NA_PILOT_AE”). Helps triage routing disputes.

Usage and intent rollup properties (MVP rollups only; keep minimal)
11. ri_usage_tokens_30d
- Type: number
- Description: Total tokens (30d) for the workspace/org mapped to the company.

12. ri_usage_tokens_7d
- Type: number

13. ri_usage_spend_usd_30d
- Type: number (currency)

14. ri_usage_spend_velocity_7d_usd
- Type: number
- Description: 7d spend velocity ($/day) as computed by analytics.

15. ri_reliability_429_count_7d
- Type: number

16. ri_reliability_error_rate_7d
- Type: number
- Description: % error rate (rounded to 2 decimals). Define denominator in scoring service; in HubSpot treat as informational.

17. ri_intent_docs_last_14d
- Type: multi-line text
- Description: Comma-separated intent events with counts.
- Example: “/docs/dedicated (3), /docs/private/vpc (1), /security/faq (2), /pricing (1)”

18. ri_account_region
- Type: enumeration (single-select)
- Values: NA | EMEA | APAC | LATAM | unknown
- Description: Used only as a fallback for routing; prefer data from billing country / self-serve signup.

19. ri_account_tier
- Type: enumeration (single-select)
- Values: self_serve | growth | enterprise | unknown
- Description: Derived; used for prioritization.

20. ri_plg_signal_outreach_status
- Type: enumeration (single-select)
- Values:
  - not_contacted
  - attempted
  - connected
  - meeting_booked
  - evaluation_started
  - opp_created
  - disqualified
  - do_not_contact
- Description: Sales-owned outcome tracking for attribution.

21. ri_plg_signal_outreach_status_last_updated
- Type: datetime

Opt-out / customer sensitivity
22. ri_plg_signal_customer_opt_out
- Type: boolean
- Description: If true, router must never create tasks/notes; only internal dashboards. This is set manually by Support/CS/Sales Ops.
- Notes: Required due to SUP-3392 class issues.

Property group: “PLG Admin (Redwood)” (restricted permissions)
23. ri_plg_signal_last_router_run_id
- Type: single-line text
- Description: Idempotency/audit reference for the last upsert.

24. ri_plg_signal_last_hubspot_task_id
- Type: single-line text

25. ri_plg_signal_last_hubspot_note_id
- Type: single-line text

Permissions guidance
- “PLG Admin (Redwood)” should be editable by HubSpot Admin + Sales Ops only.
- “PLG Signals (Redwood)” readable by Sales/CS/SE; editable by Sales for outreach status + DNC, and by router integration user for all router-managed fields.

2) (Optional / post-MVP) Custom object: PLG Signal
Not required for pilot, but define now to avoid rework.
Object name: PLG Signal (ri_plg_signal)
Associations: Company (required), Contact (optional), Deal (optional)
Recommended properties:
- ri_signal_id (string; primary key from router)
- ri_signal_type (enum; same as company last_type)
- ri_signal_score (number)
- ri_signal_confidence (enum)
- ri_signal_detected_at (datetime)
- ri_signal_window (enum: 1d | 7d | 30d)
- ri_signal_dedupe_key (string)
- ri_signal_summary (text)
- ri_signal_payload_redacted (text; optional; MUST NOT include PII; only high-level counts)
- ri_signal_status (enum: routed | suppressed | dismissed | converted)

3) Lists and views
Goal: give AEs/SDRs a “signal review queue” without building a separate UI.

Active Signal Queue (Company saved view)
Filters:
- ri_plg_signal_qualified = true
- ri_plg_signal_last_seen_at is within last 14 days
- ri_plg_signal_outreach_status is any of (not_contacted, attempted)
Sort:
- ri_plg_signal_score desc
Columns:
- Company name
- Owner
- ri_plg_signal_last_type
- ri_plg_signal_score
- ri_plg_signal_last_seen_at
- ri_usage_spend_usd_30d
- ri_reliability_429_count_7d
- ri_intent_docs_last_14d
- ri_plg_signal_last_summary

Suppressed / Monitor-only view
Filters:
- ri_plg_signal_suppressed_until is known AND is after today
OR
- ri_plg_signal_next_step = monitor_only
Columns:
- Company name
- ri_plg_signal_suppression_reason
- ri_plg_signal_suppressed_until
- ri_plg_signal_last_type

CS Expansion Candidates view
Filters:
- ri_plg_signal_last_type in (expansion_workspaces, expansion_org_invites)
- existing customer flag = true (use existing property if present; if not, define “ri_is_paid_customer” boolean from billing integration)
- ri_plg_signal_next_step = notify_csm OR owner is CSM

Marketing conflict audit list
Filters:
- ri_plg_signal_suppression_reason = marketing_nurture_conflict

4) Workflows (HubSpot automation)
Principles
- The router service is the source of truth for routing decisions; HubSpot workflows should be thin (mostly notifications, task templates, and guardrails).
- Avoid loops: changes made by workflows should not retrigger the router.
- Use a dedicated integration user for router API updates and lock down permissions.

Workflow A: “PLG Signal → Create Follow-up Task (Pilot)”
Trigger enrollment:
- ri_plg_signal_qualified becomes true
AND
- ri_plg_signal_customer_opt_out is not true
AND
- ri_plg_signal_outreach_status is empty OR = not_contacted

Actions:
1) If Company owner is unknown → assign owner based on ri_account_region (if present) else put into round-robin list (Sales Ops to define assignment rules).
2) Create Task (see task templates section) based on ri_plg_signal_last_type.
3) Set ri_plg_signal_outreach_status = not_contacted (only if empty).
4) Send internal notification (Slack/email) to owner (optional; pilot decision: email only to reduce noise).

Notes:
- Ensure re-enrollment is OFF; we do not want multiple tasks per day for the same company.
- Suppression is handled by router; HubSpot workflow should still check ri_plg_signal_suppressed_until (if set and > now, do not create task).

Workflow B: “PLG Signal → Notify CSM (Expansion / Existing Customer)”
Trigger:
- ri_plg_signal_next_step = notify_csm
OR
- ri_plg_signal_last_type in (expansion_workspaces, expansion_org_invites)
AND
- paid customer = true

Actions:
- Create internal task for CSM OR send notification to CSM team inbox (CS preference).
- Add note: “Signal suggests expansion; coordinate outreach to avoid duplicate touches.”

Workflow C: “Outcome logging reminders (Anti-stale)”
Trigger:
- Task created by Workflow A is overdue by 7 days
AND
- ri_plg_signal_outreach_status in (not_contacted, attempted)

Actions:
- Create reminder task: “Update PLG outreach status + disposition.”

Workflow D: “Do Not Contact enforcement”
Trigger:
- ri_plg_signal_outreach_status = do_not_contact OR ri_plg_signal_customer_opt_out = true
Actions:
- Close any open PLG signal tasks
- Set ri_plg_signal_suppressed_until = now + 180 days (manual override permitted)

5) Task templates
Task naming convention
- Prefix all tasks with: [PLG Signal]
- Include signal type + recommended motion (Dedicated vs Private vs monitor)

Template 1: [PLG Signal] Scale / Spend Velocity → Dedicated eval
- Applies to: scale_usage, scale_spend_velocity
- Due: 1 business day
- Notes (task body):
  - Confirm current workload (model, tokens/day, peak TPS, regions)
  - Ask about: cost sensitivity, latency SLOs, burst patterns
  - CTA: offer Dedicated capacity + benchmark plan
  - Link: Playbook section “Scale signals” (Confluence)

Template 2: [PLG Signal] Reliability (429s/latency) → Stabilize + Dedicated
- Applies to: reliability_429s, reliability_latency
- Due: same day
- Notes:
  - Acknowledge impact; ask about user-facing symptoms
  - Offer quick mitigation (rate limits, retries, batching, caching)
  - Position Dedicated for predictable throughput + isolation

Template 3: [PLG Signal] Compliance intent → Private/VPC discovery + security handoff
- Applies to: intent_private_vpc_docs, intent_security_faq
- Due: 1 business day
- Notes:
  - Discovery: data residency, retention, audit logs, SSO/SAML, KMS requirements
  - If healthcare/fintech/regulatory flags: loop SE + Security early
  - Link: Security FAQ (internal) + call scheduling guidance

Template 4: [PLG Signal] Dedicated intent (docs/pricing) → fast follow-up
- Applies to: intent_dedicated_docs, intent_pricing
- Due: 2 business days
- Notes:
  - Ask what triggered research (cost, reliability, procurement)
  - Offer sizing + rough commit ranges (stay within pricing guardrails)

Template 5: [PLG Signal] Expansion (workspaces/invites) → multi-team rollout
- Applies to: expansion_workspaces, expansion_org_invites
- Due: 2 business days
- Notes:
  - Confirm teams/use cases; propose org-wide plan
  - Coordinate with CSM if existing customer

6) Required HubSpot API scopes + integration user
Integration user
- Create a dedicated HubSpot private app (or OAuth app) for the signal router service.
- Name: “redwood-plg-signal-router”
- Store secrets in approved secret manager; rotate quarterly (or on incident).

Scopes (minimum viable)
- CRM objects: companies (read/write)
  - To search by domain / external ID and update properties
- CRM objects: contacts (read; optional write)
  - Read to locate primary contact if needed; avoid writing PII from product telemetry
- CRM objects: tasks (write)
  - Create tasks for owners
- CRM objects: notes (write)
  - Append timeline note with summary (no raw events)
- Owners (read)
  - Resolve owner IDs; route deterministically
- Pipelines / deals (read)
  - Check for open opportunities to suppress new tasks (if this logic is in HubSpot; preferred to be in router)

Rate limit considerations
- HubSpot APIs are rate limited; router must batch where possible and implement exponential backoff (see INT-1843).
- HubSpot workflows should not create cascading API calls.

7) Timeline note format (standard)
Title line:
“PLG Signal: {type} (score={score}, confidence={confidence})”
Body:
- Detected: {timestamp}
- Summary: {ri_plg_signal_last_summary}
- Rollups: tokens_7d={...}, spend_30d=${...}, 429s_7d={...}
- Recommended motion: Dedicated | Private/VPC | Monitor
- Router run_id: {ri_plg_signal_last_router_run_id}

Redaction rules
- Do NOT include: prompt text, user identifiers, IP addresses, exact endpoint paths tied to a user, or per-request logs.
- OK to include: aggregated counts, high-level docs categories, and numeric rollups.

8) Change control
- Any change to enumerations for ri_plg_signal_last_type or outreach status values must be approved by Sales Ops + Product owner (Nikhil Sharma) and documented in ADR addendum.
- Any new property that could be construed as personal data must be reviewed by Security/Privacy (Dr. Aisha Rahman / Marcus Lin) before creation.

9) Ops implementation checklist (HubSpot Admin)
Setup
[ ] Create property groups: “PLG Signals (Redwood)”, “PLG Admin (Redwood)”
[ ] Create company properties 1–25 as specified (validate types and enum values)
[ ] Set permissions: restrict “PLG Admin (Redwood)” edits
[ ] Create saved views (Active Signal Queue, Suppressed, CS Expansion Candidates)
[ ] Create task templates (5 templates) with naming convention
[ ] Create workflows A–D with enrollment criteria and re-enrollment OFF
[ ] Confirm owner routing rules (region mapping + round-robin pools) with Sales Ops
[ ] Create integration user/app “redwood-plg-signal-router”; grant minimum scopes
[ ] Confirm audit log retention and access controls for integration user

Validation (pre-pilot)
[ ] Test company lookup by domain and by external ID field (if used)
[ ] Dry run in sandbox: property upsert + note + task creation
[ ] Verify: creating/updating properties does not trigger unintended workflows
[ ] Verify: suppression fields prevent task creation
[ ] Verify: DNC/opt-out closes tasks and prevents new ones
[ ] Verify: CSM notification workflow triggers only for paid customers
[ ] Verify: timeline note format renders cleanly; no raw telemetry

Pilot launch (NA cohort)
[ ] Create a pilot list (NA self-serve cohort) and share view with pilot AEs
[ ] Confirm SDR/AEs have a place to leave disposition (ri_plg_signal_outreach_status)
[ ] Schedule weekly review of false positives + threshold tuning with Growth (Ben Carter) and Eng (Logan Wright)

Ongoing ops
[ ] Monitor HubSpot API errors/429s (via router dashboards; see ENG-7824)
[ ] Monthly audit: properties used, workflow errors, task volumes by signal type
[ ] Quarterly: rotate app secret + confirm scopes unchanged

Appendix A: Ownership + suppression alignment (summary)
- Preserve existing owner if: active deal owner exists OR company already has assigned AE/CSM owner (per routing ADR).
- Suppress task creation if:
  - ri_plg_signal_customer_opt_out = true
  - ri_plg_signal_suppressed_until in the future
  - open deal in pipeline stage beyond qualification (router preferred)
  - contacted within last X days (router preferred; X=14 pilot default)
- Marketing nurture conflict: router sets suppression reason; HubSpot should not override.

Appendix B: Reporting fields (minimum)
- Meeting booked rate by signal type: filter companies with outreach_status=meeting_booked and last_type
- Opp created rate: outreach_status=opp_created
- Time-to-first-touch: ri_plg_signal_last_seen_at → first task completion time (task timestamps)

Open questions
1) Do we need a dedicated field for “primary workspace/org id” on company for debugging? If so, place it in “PLG Admin (Redwood)” and restrict.
2) Should we store “last 3 signals” summary fields on company (vs only last)? Might be helpful but adds property sprawl. For pilot: no.
3) Marketing suppression: do we enforce suppression in HubSpot using Marketing email enrollment? Current plan: router sets suppression_reason=marketing_nurture_conflict based on shared calendar/list from Marketing Ops.

Revision notes
- 2025-06-12: Added customer opt-out field + DNC workflow following SUP-3392 learnings; clarified suppression precedence; updated rate limit guidance after INT-1843.
